name: Hopline 2.2
body:
**Reactions like every other chat app, names you can change, and a shared internet you can actually use.**

Install `Hopline.apk` below on every phone *before* you leave signal. Android 8+, Google Play services, Bluetooth and WiFi on. It updates 2.1 in place and keeps your chats. 2.1 and 2.2 phones talk to each other; the new features work fully between 2.2 phones.

### Reactions
- **Long-press any message** (text, photo, file, voice note, place, even a quote or a link) and a reaction bar springs up right over it: 👍 ❤️ 😂 😮 😢 🙏, or **+** for every emoji. The actions sit underneath: Reply, Reply privately, Copy, Save to phone, Share, Info, Send again, Delete for me.
- **Double-tap a bubble** to ❤️ it (double-tap again to take it back).
- **The pill under a bubble** shows the top reactions and a count, highlighted when one is yours. Tap it to see who reacted; tap your own row to take it back.

### Names
- **Change your name any time** (Settings or People). Everyone sees the new name, on your old messages too, and namesakes are told apart ("Sam · aaaa" and "Sam · bbbb").
- **Rename the group for everyone** from the new **Group info** screen. A line in the chat says who renamed it, and phones that were out of range pick it up when they come back.

### Tidier chats
- **Mute** a chat for 8 hours, a week or always (an @mention still gets through), **Delete for me**, and **Clear chat**.
- A chat **opens at the first message you haven't read**, with an "unread messages" marker, so backlog that hopped in after a reunion is never skipped. A "new messages above" pill catches anything that lands while you're reading history.
- Each chat keeps its own **draft and reply**, and every question (photo caption, delete, mute, place…) survives rotating the phone or Android closing the app.
- **Reply privately** from any group message, and **reply straight from the notification** (your reply now shows under their messages instead of wiping them).
- Messages that couldn't be delivered within the 48-hour carry say so honestly, with **Send again** (photos are re-sent as they were, not shrunk twice).

### Shared internet, rebuilt
- **Weather here**: one tap; your GPS works with no signal, and a phone with signal fetches a 3-day forecast for exactly where you stand.
- **Text home**: "I'm OK" to Mom with your location and the time you wrote it. Any phone with even one bar of plain mobile service can send it; its owner taps Send in their own Messages app, and Hopline asks them afterwards whether it went.
- **Look it up / read a page**: type a question or paste a link. Pages come back as clean readable text with numbered links, and "Read more" fetches the next part.
- **Ask with no signal at all.** The request travels with the group and runs the moment *any* phone gets signal, including your own. If that phone goes quiet, another takes over, except a text home, which waits for you to decide so the family never gets it twice.
- **Answers come back only to you**, with a one-tap Share to group.
- Your phone helps only while **Share my internet** is on, within a **daily allowance** you choose (texts cost no data and carry on after it runs out), never while roaming unless you allow it, with a list of exactly what it did for whom. Phones with 2.1 can still answer in the old public way, if you agree.

### Photos and files
- A **zoomable photo viewer** (pinch, double-tap, swipe down to close) with **Save to phone** (Pictures/Hopline or Download/Hopline) and **Share**.
- Safer piece storage: a phone that's nearly full says so instead of failing silently, and catches up once you free some space; pieces a phone has let go of are no longer re-sent to it over and over.

### Fixed
Over a hundred bugs, found by a line-by-line audit and an independent review. Among them:
- Messages, reactions and receipts are now saved safely in the background, so a crash or battery death no longer loses the last minutes.
- Links between phones are proven per connection, so a stranger can no longer relay a handshake, and your name is no longer sent before a phone has proved it knows the group code.
- A phone with a wrong clock can no longer lock the group's name or pin its messages to the bottom.
- On Android 8, sharing no longer treats every mobile connection as roaming.
- The radio no longer piles up retries (and drains the battery) when Play services can't advertise, and phones that failed to connect six times now try again after a rest.
- Notifications: a burst of backlog now shows the right count, two chats can never swap reply buttons, and a "please text…" request no longer lingers after it moved to another phone.
- Typo'd group codes are caught ("Did you mean *tiger river lamp*?"), and the status line says so when nearby Hopline phones are in a different group.
- Dozens of fixes for rotation, dark mode, TalkBack and right-to-left layouts.

### Honest limits (unchanged)
- No end-to-end encryption. Anyone with the 3-word code is in the group, and every phone in it carries private chats to pass them along.
- Shared internet is text only; pages that only work in a full browser say so. The person whose phone has signal can see what you asked for.
